risks.title: Persistent Inflation and Monetary Policy Tightening
risks.summary: Inflation remains elevated, prompting central banks to maintain or increase interest rates. This tightening cycle risks slowing economic growth and increasing financial market volatility.
risks.watch_for: Consumer Price Index (CPI) and Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) inflation data, Federal Reserve (FOMC) statements and interest rate decisions.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook, June 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: Geopolitical Tensions and Supply Chain Disruptions
risks.summary: Ongoing geopolitical conflicts and trade policy shifts continue to disrupt global supply chains, leading to price volatility and impacting economic activity.
risks.watch_for: Developments in ongoing conflicts, trade negotiations, and reports of supply chain bottlenecks.
sources: Wells Fargo Investment Institute (2026 Midyear Outlook, June 2026)

risks.title: AI Investment Boom and Infrastructure Strain
risks.summary: The rapid build-out of AI infrastructure is driving significant business investment but is also straining physical resources like power and skilled labor, potentially leading to increased costs and localized disruptions.
risks.watch_for: Capital expenditure announcements by tech companies, reports on infrastructure bottlenecks (power, water, equipment), and AI-related productivity gains.
sources: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (2026 Mid-Year Investment Outlook, June 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: US Fiscal Deficits and Rising Debt Servicing Costs
risks.summary: Persistent large fiscal deficits are leading to a significant increase in US national debt, with rising interest rates exacerbating debt servicing costs and crowding out other government spending.
risks.watch_for: Congressional Budget Office (CBO) deficit projections, US Treasury yield movements, and government debt-to-GDP ratios.
sources: Congressional Budget Office (CBO Finds Rising Rates Could Explode the Debt, October 2026)
CBO: FY 2026 Budget Deficit Totaled $2 Trillion, October 2026
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

risks.title: Labor Market Dynamics and Affordability Concerns
risks.summary: While the labor market shows resilience, concerns remain about slowing job growth, low labor turnover, and the impact of persistent inflation on consumer affordability, particularly for lower and middle-income households.
risks.watch_for: Monthly nonfarm payroll data, unemployment rate, wage growth, and consumer sentiment surveys.
sources: Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (Got data? Monitoring the US economy, March 2026)

risks.title: Narrowing Drivers of US Economic Expansion
risks.summary: The US economic expansion is increasingly reliant on a narrow set of drivers, primarily tech investment and wealth-driven consumer spending, making it vulnerable to disruptions in these areas.
risks.watch_for: Divergence in consumer spending patterns (high-income vs. others), trends in tech investment, and equity market performance.
sources: J.P. Morgan Asset Management (2026 Mid-Year Investment Outlook, June 2026)

risks.title: Global Growth Slowdown and Divergent Paths
risks.summary: Global growth is projected to slow, with emerging markets facing particular challenges due to geopolitical tensions and commodity price volatility, leading to divergent economic paths across regions.
risks.watch_for: IMF and World Bank global growth forecasts, regional economic updates, and commodity price indices.

risks.title: Erosion of Trust and Political Polarization
risks.summary: A decline in trust across institutions and increasing political polarization can create an unstable environment, making it harder to address economic challenges and implement effective policies.
risks.watch_for: Public opinion polls on trust in institutions, political discourse surrounding key economic issues, and outcomes of elections.
sources: KPMG (Navigating an erosion in trust, February 2026)
Stanford SIEPR (US Economy 2026: What to Watch, 2026)

consensus_note: There is a strong consensus across institutions regarding the persistent nature of inflation and the need for continued monetary policy vigilance. Geopolitical tensions and their impact on supply chains are also a widely recognized risk. However, there is some divergence on the precise impact of AI investment on productivity versus infrastructure strain, and the extent to which the US economy's growth is becoming overly reliant on a narrow set of drivers.
